title: Auditors who doubted survival or would not sign off cleanly
question: Did an auditor warn that a City-paid organization might not be able to keep operating, or decline to give a clean opinion on its accounts?
finding: 5 audit reports of City-paid organizations include a going-concern paragraph and 6 carry a qualified opinion on the financial statements.
how: Read from the yes/no fields each auditor completes when filing with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse: "going concern paragraph included" and the type of opinion on the financial statements.
limits: A going-concern paragraph is a warning about cash, not about honesty, and organizations often recover. A qualified opinion can turn on one accounting question. Only organizations large enough to need a federal audit appear.
